door_pixel_measurement.height: The lever sits at a plausible adult waist or hip height.
door_pixel_measurement.panel_placement: The rose and spindle remain inside the broad central wooden field. A large wood area remains between the hardware and the right jamb instead of the narrow latch-side strip required by real lock mechanics.
door_pixel_measurement.geometry_verdict: FAIL. The left hinges and height are credible, but the complete lockset is still too far inside the slab to connect plausibly to a right-edge latch.

full_outward_u_turn_return_path.visible_evidence: A dark footprint trail begins below the lift threshold, curves broadly through the lower-left and lower-middle floor, and trends toward the door side.
full_outward_u_turn_return_path.outward_leg: FAIL. No distinct first leg can be traced from the apartment-door zone outward to the lift.
full_outward_u_turn_return_path.turn_at_lift: PARTIAL. The trail curves near the lift, but a tight reversal with two independently readable directions is not established.
full_outward_u_turn_return_path.return_leg: PARTIAL. A path from the lift area back toward the woman is readable, but it is not separated from a preceding outward leg and does not terminate cleanly at the raised heel.
full_outward_u_turn_return_path.heel_read: The raised trailing heel appears to be the woman's anatomical left heel in the mostly back-facing pose, not an unambiguous right-heel endpoint.
full_outward_u_turn_return_path.arrival_competitor: The same single path can read as muddy footprints left while she exits the still-open lift and approaches the apartment door.
full_outward_u_turn_return_path.verdict: FAIL under the full-route contract. The pixels show a curved lift-to-door path, not an unmistakable door-to-lift outward leg, tight U-turn, and separate return leg.

supporting_evidence: The lift has a real residual opening.
The woman is physically turned back toward the apartment door.
The man remains anchored at the door while only the woman has floor-path evidence.
before_departure_readability.competing_read: She may instead have exited the still-closing lift and walked toward the man at the apartment door. The single muddy-looking trail does not exclude arrival.
before_departure_readability.verdict: FAIL under a strict image-first threshold. A return is plausible, but the complete outward-U-turn-return chronology is not visually exclusive.

same_door_palm.evidence: The woman's palm is clearly on the uninterrupted center-left wood of the same fully closed brown slab that carries the lever.

body_and_limb_separation.evidence: Exactly two people are visible, with clear air between their bodies and between every action limb. No person-to-person touch, merged anatomy, duplicate, or reflection appears.

visible_text.verdict: PASS. Wording, spelling, capitalization, punctuation, and line breaks match the locked copy; one tiny top-right brandmark is present; no extra readable text appears.

unexpected_story: The woman may be arriving from a still-closing lift rather than returning to a door she had just left.
The lever may be decorative or attached to an implausible internal mechanism because its spindle remains roughly one-quarter of the door width from the latch edge.
The dark floor marks can read as muddy arrival footprints rather than neutral motion notation.
uncertainties: The right slab edge is partly occluded by the man at lever height, so its local x-coordinate is inferred from the visible edge above and below; the resulting 24-28 percent backset is large enough that this uncertainty cannot change the failure.
A single frame cannot prove that the lock was checked twice.
The man's three-quarter pose does not secure the active hand as anatomical left.

semantic_verdict.summary: The frame passes the nearly-closed far-left lift, exact copy, single brandmark, no-extra-text, same-door palm, exactly two visible hands, entirely exterior staging, and clear body separation. It still fails the creator's hard hardware gate: the lever spindle remains approximately 110-123 pixels, or 24-28 percent of the slab width, inside the right door edge. The floor marks also show only one broad curved lift-to-door trail, not a complete outward leg, tight U-turn, and separately legible return leg.
semantic_verdict.primary_failure: Ordinary door-hardware geometry: the lever remains visibly detached from the right latch-side edge and sits inside the main wooden field.
